description:
Two dump kinds were reported run-to-run nondeterministic. One is fixed; the other
survives at the RENDERING layer only, which makes it a different defect than
filed.

## Fixed: the fixpoint is deterministic

The original ticket's sharpest claim was that the settled fact content itself
wobbled -- `Kernel.dbg/1([int]|[])`'s return type flipping between `[int] | []`
and a widened `int | float | binary | atom | ... | any` across runs of
`fz_f98_range_map_converges`, i.e. a schedule-dependent ReturnType fixpoint
end-state where one state was WIDENED.

    fz2 interp fz_f98_range_map_converges.fz --dump activations   x4
    2d2f45046cf0f33c  2d2f45046cf0f33c  2d2f45046cf0f33c  2d2f45046cf0f33c

Four identical hashes. The widening flip is gone. fz-f98.19 is the likely
reason: a job's fact emission order is now preserved end to end, so two compiles
of the same input run the same jobs in the same order, pinned by
`compiling_the_same_root_twice_runs_the_same_jobs_in_the_same_order`.

The reported downstream symptoms are also gone: `enum_tier0`'s "answer
conflation" (three consecutive base runs giving three different outputs, with
the reduce sum and the count printing each other's answers) does not reproduce --
four runs, byte-identical output. Neither does the intermittent "backend expected
runtime lane 2" decode abort.

## Still true, but it is a RENDERING defect

    fz2 interp map_enumerable.fz --dump backend   x4
    e11bd656fc3b3b6f  6664c908a93db836  3972f43b2990cd05  96b0a16601d842a7

Four different hashes -- but the difference is pure ORDER:

    wc -l    49150 / 49150
    diff <(sort dump_1) <(sort dump_2)   ->  empty

Identical as a multiset of lines. The backend program's CONTENT is deterministic;
only the order the dump prints it in is not. That is `HashMap` iteration order in
the rendering, not a fixpoint wobble, and it is the same root as fz-f98.21: there
is no canonical serialization of a `BackendProgram`, so `{:?}`-derived output is
unstable even when the structs are equal (measured there: substituting `Ty(n)`
for its display rendering still yields two different 1.7M-char strings for equal
structs).

## What to do

Byte-level product fingerprinting -- the original motivation, from
fz-go4.18.28.1 -- needs a canonical rendering, which is fz-f98.21's subject. This
ticket should either fold into it or be limited to "make `--dump backend` emit in
a deterministic order", which is the same work at a smaller scope.

Do NOT reopen this as a fixpoint bug. The fixpoint half is measured green above,
and chasing it there would be chasing something that has already moved.

## Checks

- `--dump backend` produces identical bytes across repeated runs of the same
  input.
- The activations dump stays stable (it is today).
- Whatever mechanism is used is shared with fz-f98.21's canonical form rather
  than being a second renderer.

comments.text:
FOLDED INTO fz-f98.21. This ticket's own closing advice was "needs a canonical
rendering, which is fz-f98.21's subject. This ticket should either fold into it
or be limited to 'make --dump backend emit in a deterministic order', which is
the same work at a smaller scope." Taking the first option; f98.21 now carries
`--dump backend` byte-stability as an explicit check.

One correction before it goes, so the next person does not inherit it: this
ticket's diagnosis ("the difference is pure ORDER... identical as a multiset of
lines") is FIXTURE-SPECIFIC. It was measured on map_enumerable. On
00420_enum_take_drop_split the SORTED dumps also differ:

    md5 of sort(dump) x3 -> 4a153a56..., dca72f12..., 76a5f8f1...
    16 differing lines, same 309,892 line count, same byte length

The differences are `Ty(n)` ids (the dump is `{:#?}`-pretty-printed, so ids sit
on their own line -- grep 'Ty([0-9]*)' finds nothing, which is a trap). So there
is a SECOND mechanism this ticket missed: run-to-run arena renumbering, not just
rendering order. Root-caused into four clusters -- three are upstream mint-order
dependence (fz-kdt.47) and one is an interner canonicalization gap (fz-kdt.48).

The "Do NOT reopen this as a fixpoint bug" advice stands and is still correct:
program output and the entire public work sequence are byte-identical across
runs. It was the "rendering only" half that was too narrow.

title: Backend dump is run-to-run unstable in ORDER only; the fixpoint half of go4.18.28.6 is fixed
